Q: Force git stash to overwrite added files A:

The other solutions didn't work for me. Here's what I did:

git branch temp && git reset --hard stash && git reset temp && git branch -D temp

To hard-reset and then reset back changes your working tree without changing your branch.

Q: Clean/Purge an Exchange Online Mailbox using PowerShell - Post 1st July 2020 A:

New-ComplianceSearchAction can handle 10 email purges at a time. So, you have two options as I can think of

  1. Loop through many cycles of New-ComplianceSearchAction -Purge -PurgeType HardDelete
  2. Apply Retention Policy to the selected mailboxes in which the policy can delete all emails before 'x' number of days

Q: Script commands run but only after being manually run A:

It sounds like you're encountering an issue that may be related to how the scp command operates within your shell script context, especially with file permissions and the timing of operations. Here are some possible reasons for the behavior you're experiencing, along with solutions to help you troubleshoot and resolve the issue:

Possible Issues and Solutions

  1. Race Condition:

    • After executing ssh $RHOST cp -p "$CMD_DIR/$CMD" "$CMD_DIR/${CMD}_old", it's possible that the remote file system hasn't completed the operation before the scp command runs. Although this is typically fast, network latency could cause it.

    Solution:
    Introduce a small delay after the cp command before executing scp. This can be done using sleep.

    ssh $RHOST cp -p "$CMD_DIR/$CMD" "$CMD_DIR/${CMD}_old"
sleep 1  # Introduce a delay
scp -p "$CMD_DIR/$CMD" $RHOST:$CMD_DIR/$CMD.tmp

  2. Non-Interactive Mode and Environment Variables:

    • When running commands via ssh, certain environment variables and interactive shell features might not be available. This may affect how paths are resolved.

    Solution:
    Ensure that you use absolute paths and that any necessary environment setup is included in your ssh commands.

  3. File Locks or Temporary Files:

    • If another process is accessing the file during the transfer, it might cause the scp to fail.

    Solution:
    Check for any processes that may interfere with file access. Consider using unique temporary file names to avoid conflicts.

  4. Error Handling:

    • If the scp command fails but is not caught in your script, you won't know what went wrong.

    Solution:
    Add error checking after your commands to diagnose failures:

    for RHOST in $RHOSTS; do
    ssh $RHOST cp -p "$CMD_DIR/$CMD" "$CMD_DIR/${CMD}_old"
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        echo "Failed to copy on $RHOST"
        continue
    fi
    sleep 1  # Optional delay
    scp -p "$CMD_DIR/$CMD" $RHOST:$CMD_DIR/$CMD.tmp
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        echo "SCP failed on $RHOST"
        continue
    fi
    ssh $RHOST mv $CMD_DIR/$CMD.tmp $CMD_DIR/$CMD
    if [[ $? -ne 0 ]]; then
        echo "Failed to move file on $RHOST"
    fi
done

  5. SSH Configuration:

    • Ensure that any SSH configuration (e.g., DNS resolution, key access) is correctly set up for non-interactive sessions.

Conclusion

Consider implementing the recommended changes and monitoring the output from the error checks to identify the specific cause of the failure. Adding logging, error handling, and possibly introducing delays can often resolve issues related to timing and system state. If problems persist, additional debugging tools like rsync may also provide better handling for file transfers and could be worth considering as an alternative to scp.

Q: Why is cv2.resize transposing the requested dimensions? A:

Put simply, you made a mistake when you destructured the numpy array's shape: w, h, d = image.shape. That's the mistake.

The shape is (height, width, depth), so the code should have been:

h, w, d = image.shape

Q: why npm install does not respect version in package.json A:

npm has, I would say, a bug, and will refuse to downgrade a package if a newer version of that package is already installed, even if it conflicts with your requested version.

This can happen if you had a later version set in your package.json, but then you wanted/needed to downgrade it. Even if you explicitly modify your package.json and put the version you want, running npm install will not respect the package's request.

The Fix:

The fix for this is to simply remove the dependency from your package.json, run npm install, then re-add it, and run npm install again. Only this seems to work for me.
